sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:1
items.html: Ten inner Sefirot and ten surrounding ones: And one should not object that this contradicts what is written below (Chapter 6, Item 18), namely that there emerged from the Peh of AK only five inner and two surrounding. For there he speaks of general surrounding lights, but in particular there is no light that does not have in it inner and surrounding, as written in its place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:2
items.html:
The face: Meaning that two phases of lights are discerned in a complete Partzuf: the first is called the light of Hochma, and the second is called the light of Hassadim. And corresponding to them we discern in every Partzuf two illuminations: right and left, face and posterior. Right and left pertain to the illumination of the light of Hassadim; face and posterior pertain to the illumination of the light of Hochma. And it is known that the first restriction was principally upon the light of Hochma, that it should not appear in phase four; and therefore the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] were divided into face and posterior, for the phases above phase four, which receive the light of Hochma, are called face, and those that are included from phase four, which cannot receive the light of Hochma, are called posterior. And both in the face and in the posterior there are right and left: the phases that receive the light of Hassadim in abundance are called right, and those phases that do not receive the light of Hassadim in abundance are called left. Know also that the principal reckoning of the names face and posterior is discerned with respect to the Tabur, for from the Tabur upwards is called face, and from the Tabur downwards is called posterior, since the Malchut of the Guf [body] is called Tabur, as is known.
And this is what he says, “and they extend from opposite the face down to opposite the Tabur,” meaning that the expansion of these ten Sefirot from the Peh [mouth] of AK downwards extends and shines principally in the phase of the face of the Partzuf, which is above phase four that is called Tabur; but from the Tabur downwards it does not shine, on account of the restriction that rides upon phase four, as above. And even so he informs us, “and this is the principal light, but it also shines by way of the sides to all the surroundings of the Partzuf,” that is, also to the phase of the posterior within it, save that it reaches it by way of the sides, that is, from the phase of the right side and the left side. For by means of the reflected light that phase four brings into the Partzuf, which is the light of Hassadim, she is found to receive the illumination of Hochma as well, but from the phase of the light of the female, whose meaning is only to receive and not to bestow.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:3
items.html:
From the light of the left Ozen [ear] that enters the Peh [mouth]: Know that there are necessarily two phases in every vessel, which are the phase of drawing and the phase of reception (as explained in Part 3, in the Table of Answers, Item 157 and Item 158). For the coarser phase is the more excellent for the phase of drawing the light, and the reverse is the case with respect to the reception and clothing of the light, for in that the more refined is the more excellent, since it is required to be in equivalence of form with the light received in it.
Now these two phases are sometimes called upper and lower, and sometimes called internality and externality, and one must know the difference between them. The matter is that when we speak of a complete level, in which there is a phase of drawing and a phase of clothing, they are discerned by the names upper and lower. For whatever has its internality — that is, its vessel of drawing — coarser, is found to draw a higher level. For example, if its internality is phase four, it is found to clothe up to the level of Keter [crown]. It is thus found that from the standpoint of the drawing it is lower, whose meaning is coarser. And since the light of Keter requires the more refined vessel in order to be able to clothe in it, it follows that from the standpoint of the clothing it is more upper, whose meaning is that it is more refined — that is, that it has the more refined vessel, which has no like, such that it is fit to clothe the light of Keter. Therefore, when we speak of a complete level, the four phases are discerned as one above the other, that is, that whatever is more refined is more upper.
Indeed, when we speak of the phase of the vessel of drawing alone, the four phases are discerned by us like the wall of a vessel that has four shells one upon the other in its thickness, where the abundance within it is received and measured only in its innermost shell, and does not touch the three outer shells at all, and they serve in the vessel only to strengthen the innermost shell of the wall alone. So too in the vessel of drawing, we discern there the four phases as clothing one upon the other, and whatever is coarser is more internal. And phase four, which is the principal one that draws the upper light by way of coupling by striking — for the upper light is measured precisely by the level of the reflected light that she raises — is discerned as the internality of the vessel. And the remaining three phases are considered the externality of the vessel, that is, that they do not touch the light at all and do not serve it, but rather they are causes that bring about phase four, which could not be revealed without them.
And this is what he says, “from the light of the left Ozen the externality of the vessel was made,” which is phase two; “and from the aperture of the left Hotem the internality of the vessel was made,” which is phase three — that is, that whatever is coarser is more internal, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:4
items.html: And if so, how is it that from the phase of the Ozen: He raises two objections. The first: since the surrounding light is greater than the inner light, it ought to have been that the externality of the vessel should be more important than the internality of the vessel, since it serves the greater light. But in reality we see the opposite, for the internality of the vessel is the whole importance in the degree, since all the measure of its level and its vitality depends upon it; which is not so with the externality of the vessel, which has no such importance. And the second objection is: if the internality of the vessel is truly far more important than the externality of the vessel, then it ought to be drawn from a more important root, that is, from phase two of the Rosh [head], which is called Ozen [ear], and the externality of the vessel from a lower root, that is, from phase three. And why was it the reverse?

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:5
items.html: Equal in one equality: Meaning that there is no discernment in the light from its own side, but only from the phase of the vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:6
items.html: Limited within the vessel: Meaning that the measure of the illumination is limited and dependent upon the dimensions of the vessel, no less and no more; for the coarseness of phase four draws the level of Keter, and that of phase three only Hochma, and that of phase two only Bina, etc.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:7
items.html: That light which cannot enter the vessel: This is the rule: all that is received in the Partzuf is called inner light, and all that is not yet received but is destined to come into the Partzuf is called surrounding light. And Ein Sof [infinity] is the secret of the first surrounding light, which surrounds AK alone. For the coupling by striking that is made upon the screen of phase four in the Peh [mouth] of AK, whereby the great reflected light rose there and clothed the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head] of AK up to the Keter that is adjacent to and attached to Ein Sof — behold, this reflected light comprises the surrounding light of Ein Sof. For the meaning of reflected light is the whole measure of the light that is repelled from Malchut by the power of the screen. And since the measure of that repelled light is the entire difference between Ein Sof, which filled all of reality, and AK, which in relation to Ein Sof is discerned as a single thin line — behold, all this great light of Ein Sof is discerned as surrounding light to AK. Understand this. And likewise every Rosh is discerned as surrounding light to the ten Sefirot of its own Guf [body]. For by the coupling by striking in the screen that stands in the Peh of the Rosh of that Partzuf, which restrains the upper light so that it should not expand to the Malchut of that Partzuf — behold, all the light that does not enter the vessel of Malchut becomes reflected light, which clothes the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of the Partzuf, as is known. Thus this reflected light that stands in the Rosh is comprised of all that light which cannot enter the Partzuf, and which is called surrounding light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:8
items.html: And the light passes through to half the thickness of the walls of the vessel: This has already been explained above, that the four phases in the Peh [mouth] of the Rosh [head], which are from the standpoint of the vessel of drawing, are discerned there as internality and externality, similar to the wall of a vessel that has in it four shells one upon the other, where only the innermost shell is the one that touches and receives the abundance within it. And so it is with the Malchut of the Rosh, which is called Peh: the coarser phase that is there is considered the internality, that is, the one that draws the upper light, and those more refined than she are discerned as the externality, that is, that they have no direct connection with that light received there, but rather serve the surrounding light alone. And it is found that the inner light is bound and shines only from the side of the internality of the vessel, and does not touch the externality of the vessel at all; and the surrounding light goes and is revealed only by means of the externality of the vessel, and it has no contact whatsoever with the internality of the vessel. And moreover, the internality of the vessel is that which prevents the surrounding light from entering within the vessel, since it is the coarseness upon which the screen restrains, as above. And likewise the externality of the vessel is a phase of posterior to the inner light, since it diminishes its level.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:9
items.html: And its illumination would not pass over: For the light does not clothe in a vessel unless there is between them a relation of equivalence of form; and so long as there is a form discernible in the vessel over against the light, this disparity of form repels and separates the light, and does not allow it to pass within it so as to be absorbed in the vessel. And this is what he says, “for there is a great distance and difference between them,” meaning that disparity of form is what divides and distances between spiritual things, as written above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:10
items.html: That the internality of the vessel, which is the inferior: For all the greatness and excellence of the inner light lies in the greater and more inferior coarseness. And it is found therefore that the internality of the vessel, which is coarser and more inferior, is truly equal to the greatness of the inner light, which is inferior to the surrounding light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:11
items.html: In the externality of the vessel, which is the superior: For it is entirely devoid of the phase of the coarseness of the vessel that is needed for the drawing of the light, which does not apply to the surrounding light. Therefore it has a relation only with the more refined phase of the vessel, so that it should have with her a relation of equivalence of form, that is, what is needed for the clothing of the light, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:12
items.html: The surrounding light desires and wills to join with the inner light: Meaning that it desires to clothe in the internality of the vessel and to shine together with the inner light as far as is possible for it. And this is because its end is to clothe entirely in the vessel, as written above, that the meaning of inner light is what is already clothed in the vessel, and the meaning of surrounding light is what is destined to clothe in the vessel thereafter, that is, in the course of time until the end of correction.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:13
items.html:
On its outer side: He adds here a further precision: that if it did not have the more refined externality suited to the surrounding light, then the surrounding lights could never clothe in the Partzuf even in the smallest measure, “for the surrounding light would not pass through it, and the inner light would be lacking the reception of the surrounding light in it.”
And the reason for the matter is that the inner light is always drawn from above downwards to the Guf [body] only from the phase in the Rosh [head] that corresponds to it. For example, the inner light of the Malchut of the Guf is drawn from the Malchut of the Rosh, which is phase four like her. And the inner light of the vessel of ZA of the Guf is drawn from the phase of the Hotem [nose] of the Rosh, which is phase three like it. And the inner light of the vessel of Bina of the Guf is drawn from the Ozen [ear] of the Rosh, which is phase two like her. And so forth in this way. Indeed, the surrounding light is always drawn from the Sefira above the phase that corresponds to it: for the surrounding light of the Malchut of the Guf is drawn from the Hotem, which is phase three, and the surrounding light of ZA is drawn from the Ozen, which is phase two, and so forth in this way. And this is in the first expansion of Akudim, where the screen in Malchut is phase four. But in the second expansion, where the screen in Malchut is phase three, the inner light is drawn to that Malchut from the Hotem, which is likewise phase three like her, and the surrounding light for that Malchut is drawn from above the phase that corresponds to her, that is, from the Ozen, which is phase two. And so forth in this way.
And now it is well understood that Malchut cannot receive the surrounding light unless she too has a phase of vessel from above the phase in the Rosh that corresponds to her, which she acquired by her ascent to ZA, as written further on. And this is what he says, “from the light of the left Ozen,” etc., meaning that in the Partzuf AB, whose Malchut is phase three, the internality of the Peh is found to be from the Hotem, which is phase three, while the externality of the Peh is from above her phase, that is, from phase two, which is the Ozen.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:14
items.html: There is still room to object: He objects: after all, we find the externality of the vessels to be less important than the internality of the vessels, and they do not shine as they do; and if the externality of the vessels receives from the surrounding light, which is a greater light than the inner light, it ought to have been the reverse.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:15
items.html: Since it is limited within the vessel: Meaning that the level of the light is measured and limited by the greater coarseness in the vessel, such that if its coarseness were less, the measure of its light would be less. Therefore the coarseness in the vessel is found to receive a complete illumination, for the coarseness does not darken the light at all, but on the contrary it magnifies it. Therefore the internality of the vessel is exceedingly refined, although the light is small.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:16
items.html: It is not attached and restricted with the vessel: Meaning that since there is no vessel of drawing there to draw this light by way of coupling by striking, therefore the light does not clothe in its internality, as above. And therefore that light is not attached to the vessel, because the small coarseness that is necessarily found also in the externality of the vessel contains in it a disparity of form over against the wholly refined light, such that the measure of coarseness found in the externality of the vessel diminishes the light; and had it been more refined, it would have received a greater surrounding light. Therefore every external vessel is not so refined, for the coarseness in it is discerned as a great deficiency that is separated from the light and does not join with it. And therefore, although its light is great, it does not shine in the externality of the vessel as much as the inner light shines in the internality of the vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:17
items.html:
Lower in degree one than the other: For they go on diminishing on account of the refinement of the screen. For in the second Partzuf of AK, where there was in the screen only the coarseness of phase three, it was diminished from the light of Keter, and its level reached only up to Hochma.
And the third Partzuf, where there was only the coarseness of phase two, was likewise diminished from the light of Hochma, and its level was only up to Bina. And so forth in this way. And so it is also in the worlds, as written at length above in Part 3.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:18
items.html: The world of Nekudim: This is specifically in the Roshim [pl. of Rosh] of the Partzufim, from the Malchut of the Rosh upwards. Indeed, from the Malchut of the Rosh downwards, even in the first Partzuf of AK, there were no more than five inner and two surrounding, according to the words of the ARI below, Chapter 6, Item 18.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:19
items.html: From the world of Nekudim downwards: Meaning, even in the Roshim [pl. of Rosh] of the Partzufim that are after the world of Nekudim there are found no more than five inner and two surrounding. And this is by reason of the ascent of the bottom Hey to the Einayim, which is the secret of the association of the quality of mercy with judgment that is made there. And since the place of the coupling was made in the Hochma of the Rosh [head], which is the Einayim, it is found on this account that the Bina and ZA and Malchut of the Rosh went out beyond the Rosh, that is, to the phase of from above downwards, which is the phase of Guf [body]. And therefore there remained in the phase of Rosh only Keter and Hochma, as has been explained at length in my commentaries Panim Meirot and Panim Masbirot on Etz Chaim.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:5:20
items.html: There is in them no phase of surrounding lights: Meaning that the two surrounding lights, Yechida and Haya, surround also the three lower lights, NRN [Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama], but not from the phases of NRN, rather from the phases of Yechida and Haya. And know that all this is said of the general surrounding lights; indeed, in the particular surrounding lights there are always five inner and five surrounding, for there is no light that does not have in it inner and surrounding, as written in its place.
